Release it when the oil life returns to full and the Change Engine Oil message clears.
Start the engine and confirm the message stays off.
variants.note: Pontiac put the reset control in different places by model: a steering wheel button on some, the trip odometer stem on the dash on others.

variants.when: Any Pontiac with no oil life item in the menu, or when the menu reset will not hold
steps: Only run this after the oil and filter have been changed.
Turn the ignition on with the engine off; do not start it.
Press the accelerator pedal all the way to the floor and release it three times within five seconds.
Turn the ignition off, start the engine, and check whether the Change Engine Oil message is gone.
If it is still on, the reset did not take, so repeat the three pedal presses more quickly.
variants.note: This GM pedal sequence is documented across GM manuals of the Pontiac era; the five-second window is the part people miss.

variants.when: Pontiacs from about 2007 through 2010 with keyless entry, such as G5, G6, G8 and Torrent
steps: Set all four tires, and the spare if it carries a sensor, to the pressure on the Tire and Loading Information label inside the driver's door opening.
Set the parking brake and turn the ignition to ON or RUN with the engine off.
Press and hold the LOCK and UNLOCK buttons on the key fob together for about five seconds, until the horn sounds twice.
Starting at the left front tire, hold a TPMS activation tool against the sidewall near the rim at the valve stem and press its button; wait for the horn chirp.
Continue in the order left front, right front, right rear, left rear, waiting for a chirp at each corner.
Turn the ignition off after the last chirp; if a sensor takes longer than two minutes, learn mode cancels and the sequence must be repeated from the start.
variants.note: A TPMS activation tool is needed to wake each sensor. On many models the turn signal lights at the corner the car is waiting on.

variants.when: Pontiac Vibe, which does not use the GM relearn procedure
steps: Set all four tires to the pressure on the label inside the driver's door opening before anything else.
Drive the car a few miles and see whether the low pressure light goes out on its own once the pressures are correct.
Do not try the GM key fob sequence on a Vibe; its monitoring system is different and will not respond to it.
If the light stays on, have the sensor relearn done with a scan tool at a tire shop or dealer.
variants.note: The Vibe is called out in trade references as the exception to the GM procedure, but a verified step sequence for it was not available, so this stays general.

pontiac.notes: Pontiac ended production after 2010, so every one of these cars is on an older GM system; there is no touchscreen path for either reset. Earlier Pontiacs, roughly before 2007, may use a different tire monitoring setup than the fob sequence above, so check the owner's manual for the specific year.

variants.when: Ram 1500, 2500 and 3500, roughly 2019 and newer, with arrow buttons on the steering wheel
steps: Change the engine oil and filter first, then do this reset so the oil life counter matches the fresh oil.
Without pressing the brake, push the ENGINE START/STOP button once to put the ignition in ON/RUN, but do not start the engine. With a key, turn it to ON instead.
Press the down arrow on the steering wheel to scroll the cluster menu to Vehicle Info.
Press the right arrow to open Vehicle Info, then use the up or down arrow until Oil Life is highlighted.
Press and hold the right arrow until Reset appears on the Oil Life screen.
Press the down arrow to highlight Yes, then press the right arrow to confirm. The oil life returns to full.
Press the up arrow to back out, then start the truck and check that the oil change message is gone.
variants.note: On trucks with an OK button in the middle of the arrow pad, hold OK on the Oil Life screen instead of holding the right arrow.

variants.when: Older Ram trucks without a menu-driven cluster, roughly 2009 through 2018 with a turn key
steps: Change the oil and filter before you reset anything, so the service reminder is counting from the new oil.
Turn the ignition key to ON or RUN without starting the engine and without pressing the brake pedal.
Press the accelerator pedal all the way to the floor slowly, let it up, and do that three times inside ten seconds.
Turn the ignition back OFF, then start the truck and confirm the oil change message no longer shows.
variants.note: This is the Stellantis pedal method. Exact steps vary by model year, so if the message stays, try the Vehicle Info menu reset above.

variants.when: All Ram trucks with the factory tire pressure monitor. There is no reset button for this light
steps: Set the pressures first. With the tires cold, inflate all four to the cold pressure printed on the sticker in the driver's door opening, not to the number molded in the tire sidewall.
If your truck has a full-size spare that is monitored, set it to the same door-sticker pressure.
Look at the cluster tire graphic. The low tire is called out in a different color with an Inflate To message that names the target pressure.
If you are filling warm tires, you may need to add up to 4 psi over the door-sticker number for the system to see the tire as full.
Drive the truck normally. It can take up to 20 minutes of driving above 15 mph before the sensors report in and the light goes out on its own.
Recheck the pressures cold the next morning and bleed off any extra air you added to warm tires.
variants.note: Ram has no in-cab TPMS reset. Correct the pressures and the system clears itself.

variants.when: Any Ram where the light stays on or blinks after the tires are set to the door-sticker pressure
steps: Confirm all four tires, and the monitored spare, really are at the door-sticker pressure with your own gauge.
If the light blinks at every start, that is the system telling you it has a fault, not that a tire is low.
Expect a dead sensor battery, a damaged sensor, or a sensor that was not programmed after new wheels or tires.
Have a shop read the sensor IDs with a TPMS tool and relearn or replace the bad sensor. This part cannot be done from the driver's seat.

ram.notes: Ram oil change reminders are mileage and driving based, not an oil quality sensor, so the reset only tells the truck you did the work. Diesel trucks also track an exhaust filter service that is separate and is not reset this way.

variants.when: Models from about 2020 on with the large center touchscreen (Outback, Legacy, Ascent and newer)
steps: Change the oil and filter first, then do this only after the fresh oil is in the engine.
Turn the ignition to ON without starting off, so the center screen wakes up.
Tap the gear or Settings icon on the center screen and look for the maintenance or service reminder list.
Open the engine oil item in that list and choose the option that marks the service as done or resets the reminder.
Confirm when the screen asks, then restart the car and check that the oil change message is gone.
variants.note: We could not confirm the exact menu wording from a Subaru manual page; on some years the list sits under Vehicle Settings instead of Settings.

variants.when: Models roughly 2014 to 2019 that show an oil change message in the dash display
steps: Finish the oil and filter change first, then turn the ignition to ON with the engine off.
Use the info or display button on the steering wheel to page the dash display over to the oil change message.
Clear or acknowledge the message from that display, then start the engine.
Watch the next few startups: on most of these cars the message is only a mileage reminder, so once dismissed it should stay away.
variants.note: Exact button and menu steps vary by model and year and we could not verify one sequence from a Subaru source, so follow the display prompts rather than a fixed sequence.

variants.when: Models before about 2014, which mostly have no oil life monitor at all
steps: Change the oil and filter first, then write the mileage on the service sticker.
Turn the ignition to ON and look at the dash: most Subarus of this era have nothing to reset.
If an old green maintenance reminder light stays on, have a shop clear it, since it is cleared at a connector behind the dash and not with a button.

variants.when: Most Subaru models from about 2008 on, which have no tire pressure reset button
steps: Set all four tires to the pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker first, with the tires cold.
Check the spare too if your car shows a pressure for it, which only some newer models do.
Start the engine and leave it running for about twenty seconds so the system reads the sensors.
Drive at a steady speed above about twenty miles an hour for ten minutes or so.
The low tire pressure light should go out on its own; if it stays on, one tire is still low or a sensor has failed.
variants.note: Subaru does not give the driver a relearn button on these cars, so there is no button sequence to perform.

variants.when: After new tire pressure sensors, a second set of wheels, or a light that will not go out
steps: Confirm all four tires are at the door sticker pressure and the light still will not clear.
Understand that new sensor ID numbers have to be written into the car, which no in-car button can do.
Take the car to a tire shop or dealer and ask them to register the sensor IDs with a TPMS scan tool.
Ask them to also check for a dead sensor battery, which is common on sensors more than about seven years old.

subaru.notes: Subaru does not use an oil life monitor on most of its cars, so the oil message is usually a simple mileage reminder. A flashing tire pressure light that then stays on means the system has a fault, not low air, and needs to be scanned.

variants.when: All Tesla models — there is no engine oil service, so there is no oil light to reset
steps: Understand first that a Tesla is electric: it has no engine oil, no oil filter and no oil life monitor, so there is no oil change reminder to reset.
What a Tesla does show is a Maintenance list on the touchscreen, and each line is marked off only after that work has actually been done.
With the car awake and in Park, tap the Controls icon at the bottom left of the touchscreen.
Tap Service, then Maintenance, to see the list of items and when each was last recorded.
Tap the item you just completed, such as the cabin air filter or the wiper blades.
Tap Record, then Confirm, and the entry updates to today so the due-soon or overdue flag clears.
For a tire rotation, tap Tire Rotation, tap Record, choose the tire season and service type, then tap Reset.
variants.note: Tesla keeps these records for the owner's benefit, so log work an independent shop did yourself. Menu wording shifts slightly between software versions.

variants.when: Any model showing a Service, battery or vehicle alert that the Maintenance page will not clear
steps: Tap the alert banner on the touchscreen to read the full message before trying to clear anything.
Check Controls, then Service, to see whether the message is a logged alert rather than a maintenance interval.
Understand that alerts about the high voltage or low voltage battery and similar system faults come from a self-check, not a mileage timer, so no menu resets them.
Arrange service for the warning and leave the message in place until its cause has been fixed.
Do not try to clear it by resetting a maintenance interval or by rebooting the screen, because the alert will return as long as the condition is present.
variants.note: A touchscreen reboot, holding both scroll wheels until the screen goes black, clears a frozen display only, not a genuine alert.

variants.when: Model 3, Model Y, Cybertruck and Model S or Model X built roughly 2021 and newer
steps: First set all four tires to the cold pressure on the Tire and Loading Information label on the driver's door pillar, with the car parked at least three hours and not driven.
Put the valve caps back on, then wake the car and tap the Controls icon on the touchscreen.
Tap Service to see the live pressure reading for each corner, and compare them to the label figure.
Drive the car above fifteen miles an hour for a few minutes; the amber tire pressure warning stays lit until the sensors report the corrected pressures.
If a corner still reads blank or low after that drive, park, recheck that tire with a gauge, then drive again so it can report.
There is no sensor reset menu on these cars: new or rotated sensors pair themselves while you drive, so no button sequence is needed.
variants.note: Cold weather alone drops pressure and will trip the light, so check pressures on the first cold morning of the season before assuming a leak.

variants.when: Model S and Model X built roughly 2020 and earlier, and early Model 3 cars with a Reset Sensors menu
steps: Inflate all four tires to the cold pressure on the door pillar label first, then refit the valve caps.
With the car on and in Park, tap Controls, then Settings, then Service and Reset.
Tap Tire Pressure Monitor, tap Reset Sensors, and pick the wheel size that is actually on the car.
Tap Reset, then OK, and leave the car sitting still for at least twenty minutes so the old readings time out.
Drive above twenty five miles an hour; the learning runs while you drive and can take up to twenty minutes to finish.
When it finishes, a pressure shows for every wheel and the warning clears; if it is still there after the drive, run the reset once more.
variants.note: Picking the wrong wheel size sets the wrong target pressure and causes false warnings, so confirm the size before tapping Reset.

variants.when: Any model where the tire pressure icon flashes at startup or the warning keeps coming back
steps: Set all four tires to the door pillar label pressure first and drive the car, so a simple low tire is ruled out.
Watch the icon when you first power up: a flash lasting about a minute means the system has found a sensor fault, not a low tire.
Note that a dead sensor battery, a sensor damaged during a tire change, or a wheel fitted with no Tesla sensor all read as a fault.
A fault like this needs a shop with a tire pressure sensor tool to test each sensor and read the stored codes; stop here and book the car in.
Tell the shop which wheels and tires are fitted, because the car has to be told the wheel size for the pressure targets to be right.
variants.note: Resetting sensors will not fix a fault and is not a way to silence a real low tire warning.

tesla.notes: A Tesla has no oil change, no spark plugs and no timing belt, so the only resets an owner does are the Maintenance log entries and, on older cars, the tire pressure sensors. Newer cars learn their sensors by being driven.

variants.when: Most models from about 2014 on, with a digital multi-information display between the gauges
steps: Do this only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed; the reminder is just a distance counter and clearing it early only hides the next due date.
Turn the ignition to ON without starting the engine. With push-button start, keep your foot off the brake and tap the power button twice.
Use the arrow buttons on the steering wheel to scroll the display between the gauges to the gear-shaped Settings icon.
Press OK to open it, then move to Vehicle Settings and hold OK until the sub-menu opens.
Choose Scheduled Maintenance, or Oil Maintenance if your display lists that separately.
At the Reset Data? prompt choose Yes and press OK.
Turn the ignition off and back on and confirm the MAINT REQD or Maintenance Required message is gone.
variants.note: Menu wording shifts a little by model and year; look for Vehicle Settings first, then whichever item is named for maintenance.

variants.when: Older models with an analog odometer and a physical trip meter button, roughly 2013 and earlier
steps: Finish the oil and filter change first, then reset the light so the next interval counts from the right mileage.
Turn the ignition to ON and press the ODO/TRIP button until the display shows Trip A.
Turn the ignition back off.
Hold the ODO/TRIP button down and, while still holding it, turn the ignition to ON without starting the engine.
Keep holding until the trip display runs down to zeros and the MAINT REQD light flashes and then goes out.
Release the button and switch the ignition off.
variants.note: This trip-meter method only works on clusters with a real trip meter button; the exact button name and location vary by model year.

variants.when: Models with a tire pressure warning reset switch, usually low on the dash or under the steering column
steps: First set all four tires, and the spare if it carries a sensor, to the cold pressure printed on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Park somewhere safe and switch the vehicle off; the system will not initialize while the car is moving.
Turn the ignition to ON without starting the engine.
Press and hold the tire pressure warning reset switch until the tire pressure warning light blinks slowly three times, then release it.
Drive at about 25 mph or more for roughly ten minutes so the system learns the corrected pressures.
variants.note: The switch sits below the steering wheel on most cars, and low in the dash or near the glove box on some trucks and vans.

variants.when: Newer models with no reset switch, where tire settings live in the multi-information display
steps: Correct all four tire pressures, plus a monitored spare, to the door-sticker cold figure before you touch anything inside the car.
Turn the ignition to ON without starting the engine.
Use the steering wheel arrows to open the gear-shaped Settings menu on the display between the gauges.
Select Vehicle Settings, then the TPMS or tire pressure item.
Press and hold OK until the tire pressure warning light blinks three times.
Drive at about 25 mph or more for about ten minutes for the light to clear.
variants.note: Many newer Toyotas relearn on their own after a short drive once the pressures are right, with no menu step at all.

toyota.notes: Toyota's MAINT REQD reminder counts miles, it does not measure oil condition, so it will come back on schedule whether or not the oil was changed. A tire pressure light that blinks for about a minute and then stays solid is a system or sensor fault, not low air, and no reset sequence will clear it.

variants.when: Most models from about 2015 onward with a color driver display and steering wheel menu buttons
steps: Only reset the reminder after the oil and filter have actually been changed, with the car parked.
Turn the ignition to ON without starting the engine.
Use the arrow and OK buttons on the steering wheel to open the Settings menu in the instrument cluster display.
Scroll to Service and press OK.
Select the oil change or service entry, choose Reset, and press OK.
Press OK once more to confirm; the display should show a full interval again.
variants.note: On models where the service menu lives on the touchscreen instead, the same reset sits under Car, then Settings, then Service. Menu wording varies by model year.

variants.when: Models roughly 2006 through 2015 with a trip computer and a Settings menu
steps: Change the oil first; the reminder is only a counter and resetting it early hides a real service.
Turn the key to ON without starting the engine.
Open the Settings menu with the button on the end of the wiper stalk, or with the menu buttons on the steering wheel.
Scroll to Service and press OK.
Choose Reset and press OK, then press OK again to confirm.
variants.note: Some cars of this era label the entry Service Interval or Oil Change rather than Service.

variants.when: Older models with a 0.0 or SET trip reset button and a separate clock button on the cluster
steps: With the oil already changed and the ignition off, press and hold the 0.0 or SET trip reset button on the instrument cluster.
Keep holding it while you turn the ignition to ON without starting the engine.
Release the button once the service message appears in the display.
Press the clock or minute button once; the service display should clear.
variants.note: Button names and positions differ between clusters. On a number of 2010 and newer Volkswagens the interval can only be reset with a scan tool, so if no in-car method works, that is why.

variants.when: Most models from about 2012 onward, where tire pressure settings live in the display or touchscreen
steps: First set all four tires to the pressure printed on the sticker in the driver's door opening, with the tires cold.
Turn the ignition to ON and leave the car parked.
Open the Settings or Car menu in the instrument cluster display or on the touchscreen.
Select Tires or Tire Pressure.
Choose Store or Set to save the current pressures as the new reference, and confirm.
Drive normally for at least twenty minutes so the system learns the new values.
variants.note: Most Volkswagens sold here use an indirect system that watches wheel speed rather than reading sensors, so it has to be re-taught after any pressure change, rotation or tire swap.

variants.when: Models with a physical SET button marked with the tire pressure symbol on the console or dash
steps: Set all four tires to the door sticker pressure first, while the tires are cold.
Turn the ignition to ON without starting the engine.
Press and hold the SET button until the display or the warning light confirms the new pressures are stored.
Release the button and drive normally so the system can finish learning.
variants.note: Volkswagen's own guidance is to store the corrected pressures either with the set button or through the menu display, whichever your car has.

variants.when: Models with real pressure sensors in the wheels, such as the Touareg, after new sensors or wheels
steps: Set all four tires to the door sticker pressure first.
Turn the ignition on and open the tire pressure page to see whether a separate pressure is listed for each tire.
If individual pressures are listed, the car reads real sensors, and new sensors must be matched to the car electronically.
Have a tire shop or dealer run the sensor relearn with a scan tool; there is no button sequence that will do this.
variants.note: Simply correcting pressures on these cars still only needs the store or SET step. Only new sensors or a new set of wheels needs the shop.

volkswagen.notes: Because most Volkswagens use an indirect tire pressure system, the light comes back if you only add air without storing the new pressures. Resetting an oil reminder changes the counter and nothing else, so follow the maintenance schedule rather than the light.
